# niji

> PII guardrails for Claude Code and Codex, for Rails apps. niji traces the columns that identify a person (declared once in PERSONAL_ATTRIBUTES on the model) to every view, mailer, helper, controller and service, gives each read a verdict about who is looking (own, admin, recipient, allowed, exposed), and fails the build on a read nobody has reviewed.

To add niji to a Rails app, follow skills/niji-install/SKILL.md. After the install, the app's agent uses skills/niji/SKILL.md for daily work.

## Install

- [Install skill](skills/niji-install/SKILL.md): step-by-step install for a coding agent.
- [README](README.md): what niji does, install by hand, verdicts, the allowlist.

## Use

- [niji skill](skills/niji/SKILL.md): run the check, triage findings, fix leaks, write allowlist entries.
- [Configuration](docs/configuration.md): every option and its default.
- [Agents](docs/agents.md): Claude Code Stop hook, Codex, JSON output, tests and CI.

## Understand

- [How it works](docs/how-it-works.md): sources, holders, reads, relays, admin-only controllers, mail recipients, verdicts, limits.
- [The review email that named the wrong person](articles/origin-story.md): why niji exists.
- [How to stop Claude from leaking personal data into your app](articles/how-to-stop-claude-from-leaking-pii.md)
- [Four guardrails for personal data in agent-written code](articles/guardrails-to-detect-pii-in-agent-generated-code.md)
